subject: math

objective.text: See that each place value unit is 10 times the unit to its right. Write it as an equation.

explanations.title: 10 times as much
explanations.text: 10 ones make 1 ten. We say 1 ten is 10 times as much as 1 one.

explanations.title: The pattern of tens
explanations.text: 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred. 10 hundreds make 1 thousand. Each unit is 10 times as much as the unit to its right.

explanations.title: Write it as an equation
explanations.text: Show 10 times as many with an equation. For example, 10 × 2 ones = 20 ones = 2 tens.

explanations.title: Ways to model 10 times as many
explanations.text: You can model it with money, blocks, disks, drawings, dots or a tape diagram.

examples.title: 10 times 2 ones
examples.text: 10 × 2 ones = 20 ones = 2 tens. Bundle 10 ones into 1 ten, twice.

examples.title: 10 times 9 hundreds
examples.text: 10 × 9 hundreds = 90 hundreds = 9 thousands. This skips the extra step.

hints.text: Think of the multiplication fact with the same numbers.
Bundle the smaller units into one larger unit. Count how many you bundle.
Say the number with its unit. For example, say 3 ones, then bundle.
Compare a unit to the unit on its right. How many copies fit?
Multiply the number by 10. Think of 10 copies.
Add the four sides. Or add the length and width and double it.
Multiply the length by the width.
Say each digit with its unit, like 2 thousands 3 hundreds.
